tags.gloss: Asks whether a proposition is true; expects yes/no (or equivalent).
tags.watchFor: vs checkQuestion: use checkQuestion if the asker already leans toward believing it's true and is just double-checking (often tagged “...right?”).

tags.gloss: Asks which element(s) of an open set have some property (a WH-question).
tags.example: “What time does the meeting start?” / “How far is it to the station?”
tags.watchFor: vs choiceQuestion: only use choiceQuestion if the question offers an explicit closed list of alternatives to pick exactly one from.

tags.gloss: Asks which one of an explicit list of alternatives is true; expects exactly one to be picked.
tags.example: “Should the cable go in the phone line or the external line?”
tags.watchFor: vs setQuestion: needs an explicit list of options, not an open-ended what/who/where.

tags.gloss: Asks whether a proposition is true, but the asker already leans toward believing it.
tags.watchFor: vs propositionalQuestion: the tell is a tag like “...right?” / “...isn't it?” signaling the asker's prior belief.

tags.gloss: States something as fact, not in direct response to a question.
tags.watchFor: vs answer: use answer instead if it's a direct response to a preceding question.

tags.gloss: Provides information that was specifically asked for.
tags.example: Q: “What does the display say?” A: “Send error, document ready.”
tags.watchFor: Only follows a question act (propositionalQuestion / setQuestion / choiceQuestion / checkQuestion).

tags.gloss: States a proposition is true, aligning with a claim/opinion the addressee holds - not primarily a reply to a check/prop question.
tags.watchFor: vs confirm: confirm specifically answers a check/propositional question; agreement is aligning with a stated claim or opinion.

tags.short: I think that's false (re: a claim)
tags.gloss: States a proposition is false, contradicting a claim/opinion the addressee holds.
tags.watchFor: vs disconfirm/correction: disconfirm answers a check/prop question negatively; correction supplies the replacement correct info.

tags.gloss: Says previously-assumed info is wrong and supplies the correct info instead.
tags.watchFor: Must include the corrected fact itself, not just a bare “no.”

tags.short: Yes, that's right (re: a check/prop question)
tags.gloss: Confirms a proposition the addressee was uncertain about is true.
tags.watchFor: Response to checkQuestion/propositionalQuestion specifically.

tags.short: No, that's wrong (re: a check/prop question)
tags.gloss: Tells the addressee a proposition they were uncertain about is false.
tags.watchFor: Response to checkQuestion/propositionalQuestion specifically; if you also supply the right info, consider correction instead.

tags.gloss: Signals willingness/ability to do something, conditional on the addressee's consent.
tags.example: “I will look that up for you.”
tags.watchFor: vs suggest: offer is self-committing (“I will...”), suggest proposes that the other party act.

tags.gloss: Commits to an action only if a stated condition is met (response to a request/suggestion/offer).
tags.example: “If you push the bag to me.”
tags.watchFor: Must state an explicit condition; an unconditional commitment is accept instead.

tags.gloss: Unconditionally commits to a requested/suggested action, or takes up an offer.
tags.watchFor: Response to request/suggest/offer only.

tags.gloss: Refuses a requested/suggested action, or turns down an offer.
tags.watchFor: vs disagreement: decline refuses an action; disagreement rejects a claim.

clusters.name: Directive
clusters.subtitle: asking the other party to act

tags.gloss: Asks the addressee to perform an action, conditional on their consent.
tags.watchFor: vs suggest: request is more directive/imperative; suggest is framed as being in the addressee's own interest.

tags.gloss: Proposes an action the speaker believes is in the addressee's interest.
tags.example: “Let's wait for the speaker to finish.”
tags.watchFor: Softer, more collaborative framing than request.

tags.gloss: Signals successful processing/understanding of what was just said - a backchannel, not agreement with content.
tags.watchFor: vs agreement/confirm: autoPositive just says “I heard/understood,” it doesn't assert the content is true.

tags.gloss: Signals a processing problem understanding the prior utterance.
tags.watchFor: About comprehension failure, not disagreement with content.

tags.gloss: Buys time to construct a response or pause the dialogue briefly.
tags.watchFor: Pure time-buying filler, not yet a real speech act.

tags.gloss: Withdraws/abandons something the speaker just started saying, within the same turn.
tags.watchFor: Mid-utterance self-interruption/abandonment - distinct from correction, which fixes a previous turn's info.

tags.gloss: Signals presence/awareness of the addressee, typically opening a dialogue.
Signals this is the speaker's final contribution, typically closing a dialogue.
Expresses gratitude for something the addressee did.
tags.watchFor: vs acceptThanking: this is the one giving thanks, not receiving it.

tags.gloss: Response that plays down the addressee's expressed gratitude.
tags.watchFor: vs thanking: this is the reply to being thanked, not the thanks itself.

tags.gloss: Signals regret about something, seeking acknowledgment.
tags.watchFor: vs acceptApology: this is the one apologizing, not accepting the apology.

tags.gloss: Response that plays down the addressee's expressed regret.
tags.watchFor: vs apology: this is the reply to an apology, not the apology itself.

tags.short: Doesn't clearly match any of the 27
tags.gloss: Use only when a sentence clearly does not perform any of the 27 CAMS acts and does not form a speech act at all.
tags.watchFor: Last resort - re-check the 27 tags above before reaching for this.
